statement: Matrices $M$ and $N$ are shown below. $$M = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad N = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ What is the determinant of the product $MN$?

choices.misconception: I found $\det M = 14$ and $\det N = 5$ and added them, thinking the determinant of a product is the sum of the determinants.
I multiplied matching entries to get $\begin{bmatrix} 6 & -1 \\ -10 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, as if matrix products work entry by entry, and its determinant is $-10$.
I found each determinant as $ad + bc$ instead of $ad - bc$, getting 10 for $M$ and $-5$ for $N$, and multiplied them to get $-50$.

hints: You can multiply the matrices first, or use the fact that the determinant of a product is the product of the determinants.
For $\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$ the determinant is $ad - bc$. Find $\det M$ and $\det N$.

solutions.reliable: Multiply each row of $M$ by each column of $N$: $MN = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 5 & 3(-1) + 1 \cdot 0 \\ -2 \cdot 2 + 4 \cdot 5 & -2(-1) + 4 \cdot 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 11 & -3 \\ 16 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$. Its determinant is $11 \cdot 2 - (-3)(16) = 22 + 48 = 70$.
